title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
subtitle: Garlic, olive oil, and chilli
excerpt: One of the great Roman midnight pastas: spaghetti tossed in olive oil that has been gently coaxed with sliced garlic and dried chilli, finished with a handful of parsley. Made correctly it is silky and vibrant, not greasy.

recipe.sourceNotes: Spaghetti aglio e olio is a Roman dish and one of the simplest pasta preparations in Italian cooking. It is the classic after-theatre or late-night dish in Rome and Naples, made from store-cupboard ingredients when little else is available. The name simply means spaghetti with garlic and oil. The technique of using pasta cooking water to emulsify the oil into a sauce is central to the dish.

content.text: The garlic must be gently coaxed in the oil, never fried hard. It should turn pale golden over low heat while the oil absorbs its flavour. Remove the pan from the heat the moment the garlic colours, as the residual heat will continue cooking it. The pasta cooking water is the key to the sauce: it contains starch that helps emulsify the oil into a light, coating consistency rather than a puddle of grease.
Cook the spaghetti in a large pan of heavily salted water until al dente. Reserve 200 ml of the pasta cooking water before draining.

About 5 minutes before the pasta is ready, put the olive oil and sliced garlic in a large frying pan over very low heat. Cook gently for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until the garlic is pale golden and fragrant. Add the chilli flakes and cook for 30 more seconds, then remove from the heat.

Add the drained spaghetti to the pan with the garlic oil. Add 100 ml of the pasta water and toss vigorously over medium heat for 2 minutes until the oil and water emulsify into a light sauce that coats the pasta. Add more pasta water if needed to loosen.
Remove from the heat. Add the parsley and toss through. Taste and add salt. Serve immediately.
